c.tagline: Mindanao's orderly gateway city — durian, Philippine eagles, Samal Island and towering Mount Apo.

taxi.fareNote: Davao strictly enforces taxi meters and its drivers are widely known for honesty and for returning lost belongings; Grab and the local Micab app are also widely available.

emergency.note: 911 is the nationwide emergency number; Davao also runs its own Central 911 command center, one of the first in the country, with generally good English response.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Well-policed city, but wider Mindanao has security risks — check advisories

hood_desc: The historic downtown core around San Pedro Cathedral, People's Park, the City Hall and the old public markets; the central, walkable base for first-timers who want the city's landmarks, government offices and cheapest eats close at hand.

The business and shopping spine along J.P. Laurel Avenue north of downtown, anchored by the Abreeza Ayala mall and lined with hotels, offices and restaurants; a convenient, upscale-leaning base within easy reach of the center.

The upmarket coastal district northeast toward the airport, home to SM Lanang Premier, beachfront hotels and the Insular waterfront; a quieter, resort-and-mall area popular with business and leisure visitors.

A busy residential and dining district south of downtown around Matina Town Square and the Torres Street strip, known for its night market, bars and casual restaurants; a lively, local place to eat and go out.

The compact old Chinatown around Uyanguren (Ramon Magsaysay Avenue), packed with Chinese-Filipino eateries, durian stalls, temples and bustling street commerce; a flavorful, walkable pocket for food and shopping.

water.note: Davao's tap water is rated among the Philippines' best and is generally safe, though sensitive stomachs may prefer bottled.

transit.hours: Jeepneys and the new city buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 10:00 PM; late at night, taxis, Grab and Micab are the reliable options.
transit.note: Davao has no rail or metro; public transport is built on jeepneys and, increasingly, the modern High Priority Bus System (HPBS) that is replacing many old routes, supplemented by metered taxis and Grab.
transit.pay: Jeepney and bus fares are paid in cash to the driver or conductor (fares start around 13-15 pesos); there is no city-wide smartcard yet, while Grab and Micab are paid in-app or in cash.

bus: Ecoland and Davao Overland terminals to Mindanao cities
ferry: Barges and boats to Samal Island (IGaCoS) from Sasa and Sta. Ana wharves
Passenger ferries across the Davao Gulf

transit.m: Airport taxi or Grab to downtown (20-30 min)
Jeepney from the main road to the city center (longer, with a transfer)

tip.r: Tipping is appreciated but modest; leaving around 10% at restaurants without a service charge, and small change for guides, drivers and hotel staff, is customary.
